cold_open.hook: Treasury yields just hit 5% again—and the Fed's about to make it worse.

markets.macro_note: Rates climbing on inflation fears and Waller hawkishness; tech rotation away from mega-cap AI plays into chipmakers with actual revenue.

big_story.story_title: 10-year Treasury yield races back to 5% as inflation data, Waller comments drive rate hike expectation
big_story.angle: The bond market is pricing in rate hikes that the Fed hasn't signaled yet—and it's not because inflation is actually accelerating, it's because Waller's rhetoric gave traders permission to front-run the narrative.

quick_hits.angle: CoreWeave's beat and raise proves there's real AI infrastructure demand underneath the hype—not just token-buying by LLM labs trying to justify their valuations.

All seven Anthropic founders cashing out $250M each in the IPO is the most honest signal yet: they built something, they're taking chips off the table, and they're not pretending this is a 50-year mission.
Sony killing Fairgames is the live-service graveyard getting another headstone—turns out you can't just throw $200M at a multiplayer shooter and expect it to compete with free-to-play incumbents.
Credit card debt at record highs while rates stay elevated means consumers are borrowing to tread water, not to spend—that's the recession signal nobody wants to name.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Children's Place is filing for bankruptcy because there aren't enough children—which is either the most honest retail obituary ever written or the setup to a genuinely dark joke about demographics.
